title: Prince Archie Celebrates Seventh Birthday Amid Royal Family Tension
text:
Meghan Markle shares rare baby photos of Prince Archie for his 7th birthday, highlighting the complex relationship between the Sussexes and the British monarchy.
Meghan Markle has delighted fans by sharing a collection of rare and intimate photographs of Prince Archie to commemorate his seventh birthday. The Duchess of Sussex utilized Instagram to showcase previously unseen moments, including a poignant image of the young royal fast asleep on Prince Harry s chest and another heartwarming shot of Archie alongside his younger sister, Princess Lilibet, enjoying a day at the beach.
Accompanied by a sweet caption stating that seven years have passed, the post highlights the tender bond between the parents and their eldest child. These rare glimpses into their private life in California provide a contrast to the highly scrutinized public image of the royal family and offer a glimpse into the quiet moments of their domesticity.
Reflecting on the circumstances of Archies birth on May 6, 2019, the couple notably chose the private Portland Hospital in London over the traditional Lindo Wing at St Marys Hospital. This decision was the first of many steps the Sussexes took to distance themselves from rigid royal conventions, as they also declined the customary press photo call. One of the most debated aspects of Archies arrival was his initial lack of a title.
Meghan originally announced that her son would be a 'private citizen', expressing a desire for him to grow up without the constraints of historical expectations or royal protocol. At the time, they hoped he would simply be known as Mister Archie, aiming to secure a childhood defined by privacy and normalcy, a goal supported by figures like biographer Omid Scobie who noted it was all part of a larger plan for a standard upbringing.
However, the landscape changed in 2022 when King Charles III ascended to the throne. Because Archie and Lilibet are now the grandchildren of the reigning monarch, they automatically gained the titles of Prince and Princess. While Harry and Meghan have embraced these birthrights for now, they are reportedly committed to allowing their children to decide for themselves whether to retain or relinquish these titles upon reaching adulthood.
This flexibility underscores their ongoing struggle to balance their royal heritage with their desire for a modern, independent lifestyle in Montecito, ensuring their children are not bound by the weight of a crown they did not ask for. Despite the celebration, a shadow of familial estrangement looms over the occasion. Reports suggest that King Charles feels a profound sense of loss regarding the distance between himself and his California-based grandchildren.
Royal commentator Michael Cole noted that the King acutely feels the lack of closeness, perhaps mirroring the emotional voids created by his own parents' frequent absences during his childhood. While Charles maintains a very active and loving relationship with Prince Williams children—George, Charlotte, and Louis—his interaction with Archie and Lilibet has been extremely limited.
It is understood that the monarch is eager to rebuild these bridges, viewing the innocent children as a source of comfort, especially while he manages his own health challenges and cancer treatment. The physical distance of over 5,000 miles is compounded by the deep emotional divide and antipathy between the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and the rest of the British Royal Family. This friction has made normal family dynamics nearly impossible to sustain.
In a recent appearance in Melbourne, Australia, Prince Harry spoke candidly about his journey as a father, emphasizing that being a parent is the most significant role a man can hold. He revealed that he sought therapy prior to the birth of his children to ensure he could be the best version of himself for them, breaking cycles of generational trauma to provide a healthier environment for Archie and Lilibet.
As Archie celebrates another year of life, his upbringing remains a blend of royal legacy and a carefully curated private existence
